text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Work-related illnesses such as repetitive strain injury cost the Netherlands 16.5 billion guilders in 1995. (p1)
- IT and temporary employment sectors help boost AEX index by 25 pct in first five months of the year. (p1)
- Bank insurer Fortis Amev books 30 pct higher Q1 net, helped by results at merchant bank MeesPierson. (p1)
- Traffic and public works ministry mulling contribution to pipeline network for transport of chemicals. (p3)
- Investment climate improving for high-techs. (p7)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Dutch prime minister Wim Kok calls for plan to facilitate private investment in central and eastern Europe. (p1)
- Central planning bureau CPB'S spending power forecasts are always unreliable, according to government economists. (p1)
- Former chairman of small businesses association MKB forecasts the organisation's bankruptcy. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- U.S. president Bill Clinton reaffirms centuries of U.S.-Dutch ties. (p1)
- Mortgage guarantee body NHG calls on government to intervene to rein in excessive mortgage lending by banks. (p33)
- Government advisory body on socio-economic affairs cautions against major changes to unemployment insurance act. (p35)
TROUW
- Opposition party Christian Democrats CDA oppose combined supermarket/petrol stations (p5)
- Dutch engineering concern IHC Holland may lose Chinese order to France following The Hague's criticism of Peking's human rights policy. (p8)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Cabinet sets aside 125 million guilders to make schooling more attractive for employees. (p10)
- Telecom company Libertel fears it may collapse if government levies hundreds of millions of guilders in back tax on its mobile phones licence. (p11)
